metadata.question: On July 20, 2025 at 10:44 am local time, did the volcanic plume from Halemaʻumaʻu Crater extend more than 5 km (horizontal distance) from the summit of Hawaii’s Kīlauea volcano?

import ee
import math
ee.Initialize(project='earthsense-436113')

# 1. Geometry & Time Definitions
# Halemaʻumaʻu Crater summit coordinates
summit = ee.Geometry.Point([-155.283, 19.406])
# Create 5 km buffer for comparison
buffer_5km = summit.buffer(5000)  # 5 km in meters

# Date: July 20, 2025 at 10:44 am local time (Hawaii UTC-10 = ~20:44 UTC)
# Use ±2 hour window to account for satellite overpass timing
date = '2025-07-20'
start_time = ee.Date(date).advance(18, 'hour')  # 18:00 UTC = 8:00 am Hawaii
end_time = ee.Date(date).advance(22, 'hour')    # 22:00 UTC = 12:00 pm Hawaii

# 2. Data Acquisition - Try multiple sensors
# First try: Sentinel-5P SO2 (best for volcanic plumes)
s5p_so2 = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S5P/OFFL/L3_SO2') \
    .filterDate(start_time, end_time) \
    .filterBounds(summit) \
    .select('SO2_column_number_density')

# Check if Sentinel-5P has data
if s5p_so2.size().getInfo() == 0:
    # Try MODIS Terra for thermal anomalies (10:30 am overpass)
    modis = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MOD021KM') \
        .filterDate(start_time, end_time) \
        .filterBounds(summit)
    
    if modis.size().getInfo() == 0:
        # Try VIIRS (similar times to MODIS)
        viirs = ee.ImageCollection('NOAA/VIIRS/001/VNP02IMG') \
            .filterDate(start_time, end_time) \
            .filterBounds(summit)
        
        if viirs.size().getInfo() == 0:
            print("No satellite data available for the specified time.")
            print("<answer>C1</answer>")
        else:
            # Use VIIRS M12 band (3.7μm) for thermal detection
            collection = viirs
            plume_band = 'M12'
    else:
        # Use MODIS band 31 (11μm) for thermal detection
        collection = modis
        plume_band = 'BrightnessTemperature_Band31'
else:
    # Use Sentinel-5P SO2
    collection = s5p_so2
    plume_band = 'SO2_column_number_density'

# If we have a collection, proceed
if 'collection' in locals():
    # Get the first image
    image = collection.first()
    
    # For SO2: threshold > 0.0001 mol/m² for plume detection
    # For thermal: threshold > 320K for hot spots
    if plume_band == 'SO2_column_number_density':
        plume_mask = image.select(plume_band).gt(0.0001)
    else:
        # Thermal anomaly detection
        plume_mask = image.select(plume_band).gt(320)
    
    # 3. Check for valid pixels
    pixel_count = plume_mask.reduceRegion(
        reducer=ee.Reducer.count(),
        geometry=summit.buffer(20000),  # 20 km buffer for plume search
        scale=1000,
        maxPixels=1e9
    ).getInfo()
    
    total_pixels = list(pixel_count.values())[0]
    
    if total_pixels == 0:
        print(f"No plume pixels detected. Total pixels in search area: {total_pixels}")
        print("<answer>C2</answer>")
    else:
        # 4. Check if plume extends beyond 5 km buffer
        # Create mask for plume outside 5 km buffer
        plume_outside_buffer = plume_mask.updateMask(buffer_5km.not())
        
        # Count plume pixels outside 5 km buffer
        outside_count = plume_outside_buffer.reduceRegion(
            reducer=ee.Reducer.count(),
            geometry=summit.buffer(20000),
            scale=1000,
            maxPixels=1e9
        ).getInfo()
        
        outside_pixels = list(outside_count.values())[0]
        
        # 5. Determine if plume extends >5 km
        print(f"Total plume pixels: {total_pixels}")
        print(f"Plume pixels beyond 5 km: {outside_pixels}")
        
        if outside_pixels > 0:
            print("Plume extends more than 5 km from summit.")
            print("<answer>A</answer>")
        else:
            print("Plume does not extend more than 5 km from summit.")
            print("<answer>B</answer>")
